title: A queued 'ready' could reopen a billed job
story: Job status changes never read the current status. A queued 'ready' replayed after a close reopened a settled, billed job. Tests were green. A technician noticed in production weeks later.
entry: Job lifecycle. Append-only job_event rows. POST /jobs/{id}/transition with action ready, close, abandon, reschedule or haul. Each action updates the job and appends an event. Check: 7 service tests, 4 router tests, 2 real-database tests.
steps: A later session got 'wire the bill sheet', which is a task. Nothing in its window says a button can strand a job.
Tests were green. Nothing failed, so nothing asks. The first signal was a technician in production weeks later.
Any query names the task, not the hazard of a 'ready' replayed after 'close'.
'transition' and 'ready' match the old entry, which is the defect. The correct pattern is filed under money words and does not match.
The design does not say whether the entry goes to the session or to a subagent writing one screen.
Adapting the old entry reproduces 'dispatch on the action alone'. Nothing in it says to read the current status.
The old checks test each transition from one state. The every-action-from-every-status matrix came only with the fix. The stored check passes the copy.
No model failed. A technician noticed. The failing parts were written by top models.
The fix would be stored. Next day a red-team found its freeze parked landed writes as conflicts. Recording before the PR is ready stores the half-right version.
The 07-08 dispatcher handler predates the freeze and never stamps the bill-sent time. A new entry does not look back at existing code.

title: Evidence gate passed with zero bytes
story: A size check swallowed every error and returned 'unknown', so a technician could satisfy the evidence gate without uploading anything. Tests defaulted to 'unknown' and stayed green for 52 days.
entry: Upload size ceiling for pre-signed uploads. At finalize, read the real size with HEAD. Reject anything over the ceiling. A missing object or a temporary error returns None so the caller can fall back to the client's reported size.
steps: 'Harden media uploads' is a task. The evidence gate's integrity is not named in it.
The test fixture defaults to 'unknown' and the suite is green. Nothing fails, so nothing looks up.
The task's own words, upload, size and R2, find the entry. Retrieval works and delivers the defect.
Same problem, exact match, wrong answer. The stored text states the mix-up as the design.
The cheap model copies 'fall back on None', which the entry calls safe.
The handoff says the no-bytes case was the tested default and nothing asserted existence. The stored check certifies the copy.
No visible failure for 52 days. An adversarial audit found it. Nothing climbs.
The fix rule, None means unknown, never zero, is good. Captured at the first commit, it omits the selfie caller found an hour later.
The handle head_size fires on later diffs to that symbol. The same shape in other words, the mobile bare catch, is a word-level miss.

title: Switching on WhatsApp sending
story: The entry said the dispatcher is safe to switch on. Switching it on would send the whole job history: 36 real messages about months-old jobs. Suppressed rows are permanent.
entry: Customer messages through a transactional outbox. A cursor per consumer drains events in order. The WhatsApp consumer is consent-gated and log-only while settings are empty, so enable_dispatcher stays safe to flip.
worked: The correction, once stored, reaches the next operator before an env flip. That avoids a mass-message incident.
steps: 'Turn on WhatsApp Cloud sending' is one settings edit, no code. The owner's design speaks of problems a model solves.
Nothing fails before the flip. The flip is the failure. The other design has a route for actions. The owner's design names none.
'Enable dispatcher' is the entry's own phrase.
It returns the stored conclusion 'stays safe to flip', at the one moment it can do harm.
Acting on it sends the whole history, and suppressed rows are permanent.
No check can say 'safe to flip'. Nothing tested the seed or the age guard. A review found a test that pinned the consent leak.
The author was a top model. Nowhere higher to send it. Later audits found it.
The fix would be stored. But the 08-01 review found three defects inside the fix branch. 'Solved' was the reviewer's call.
After the fix, the action handle is the stated only route to operator hazards. It reaches the next operator.

title: Login lock that blocks a correct PIN
story: A strong model built a self-healing lock. An audit prescribed a different fix. A third strong model said the audit's fix opens 4-digit PIN guessing. Only an owner decision settled it.
entry: Login lockout. Five failures lock 30 seconds, doubling to a 15-minute cap, always self-healing. A correct PIN during a lock returns 429. Counter survives the error. Per-IP window behind the database lock.
steps: 'Fix HANDOFF A2' is a stated problem with file and line. Here the task is a problem.
Applying a fix that a document prescribes is a trigger in the other design.
The words line up: lock, correct PIN, 429.
Before the settling commit both hits are wrong. Each came from a strong model and passed its own check.
Applying A2 inverts two tests and opens 4-digit PIN brute force, finished in under an hour by a handful of IPs.
Inverted tests pass. Three strong outputs, two positions. Only an owner decision settled it. 'Equal to the strong model' has no single target.
The wrong fix is silent too. The audit was already a strong-model product. Climbing reaches the tier that wrote it.
The settling commit is a model capture: reason, owner decision and comments on both tests. It can be stored as do-not-apply with owner confirmation.
A document reference on A2 stops the next agent. CLAUDE.md already says so. The clinic's check held the same rule.

title: Opening cutoff rules for cash, pay and stock
source: Cutoff-guards session G10-20; transcript 97380a1e; GC-01, GD-01, GE-03
story: A rule passed its own tests and an Opus review. Three later root reviews found a double count, a hold that never released, and more. Two correct rules looked like either-or.
entry: Opening cutoff guards. One registry of cutoffs, readers per subject. Cash: opening is the balance at the end of the cutoff day. Refuse postings on or before it. Stock: opening is the count when the batch posts. Check: cutoff tests green.
worked: The final rule carried unchanged into the 2026-11-10 real-data switch, reused without re-derivation.
steps: G10-20 is a stated gap. Whether stock follows cash on the cutoff day was not known to be a question until GC-01 asked it.
Session tests and its own review passed. Nothing failed until a separate root review, three rounds running.
Good words exist. The deciding detail, an import posted on the count day, is in no query.
It returns a refuted cutoff rule or the half-right stock rule. Two rules, right on different sides, look like either/or.
The finding arrived at 366,229 tokens. The next call read 87,658 after compaction. A fetched entry rides into a summary.
The round-1 fix added a hold. Round 2 found the hold never released. Adapting the rule to new state made a new P1 defect.
Two Opus reviews read the same code and disagreed. The in-session test asserted the double count as correct.
All work was Opus. The working ladder was a root review per round. Nothing failed visibly, so nothing escalated by itself.
Which version is the entry: after own review, round 1 or round 2? Each passed its checks. The first rule's reasoning was compacted before the finding arrived.
The final rule, end of cutoff day for cash, pay and stock, carried unchanged into the real-data switch.

title: Correction form opened blank over a real bill
story: 'Correct the completion' opened a blank form. The server rewrites the bill from the payload, so a blank submit destroyed the bill. A bare catch treated 'offline' and 'no completion' as the same answer.
entry: Completion correction form must not wipe a bill. Load the existing completion and prefill materials, time and remarks. If the fetch fails, return: offline, a blank first completion is still valid. Check: mobile tests green.
steps: A stated problem: a blank form wipes a bill.
Tests were green. Nothing fails. The app has no screen-test harness.
A query would say prefill, offline. The governing rule is worded evidence, media counts, None.
The right rule exists and does not match. The same model wrote it 53 minutes earlier in the same PR.
The catch says 'offline, a blank first completion is still valid'. A fresh self-written rule did not stop it.
No screen test exists. Logic inside the component is asserted by nothing.
The red-team found it a day later. No model failed.
The fix found three doors, not the one the handoff described, plus a fourth route. An entry written from the audit would be incomplete.
The rule now lives as a tested pure function and in CLAUDE.md. Handles on it fire on later diffs.
